newsitem.title: USA: Netanyahu, Arafat dine alone at White House.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu, Arafat dine alone at White House.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat discussed their differences alone over lunch in the White House residence on Tuesday, the White House said.

Spokesman Mike McCurry said the luncheon began with President Clinton and Jordan's King Hussein joining Netanyahu and Arafat, but that after a time they left the Israeli and Palestinian leaders alone. The direct private meeting between the two appeared to be a promising early development in a U.S.-hosted Middle East crisis summit, whose early tone was described by McCurry as "sober".
"They are still dining now and as near as we can tell from the delegations they are prepared to stay there for some more time. They are together alone with interpreters," McCurry told reporters.

It had been planned that the leaders would leave the White House after the Oval Office meeting to resume disussions at the Blair House guest residence across the street. Instead, Clinton invited them to lunch in the White House library, then arranged for the Israeli and Palestinian to be left together.

McCurry described the discussions to date as "sober but very constructive and very helpful ... Certainly the discussions so far today have gone a long way toward reestablishing that notion of trust that must exist between the parties as they have their discussions."
Clinton called the two-day summit in a bid to rescue Middle East peace negotiations threatened with collapse becaue of renewed Israeli-Palestinian violence.
